claims.text: The deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The GPS polyline runs 28.9 km between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event against a booked optimal of 24.0 km — an excess of 4.9 km, or 20.42% of optimal. Both limbs of the establishment test are passed: the excess is greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure and expressly forbids citing the rounded trip_record copy for the threshold test; here the two agree at 28.9 km, so the finding is safe either way.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: coverage is 100%, there are 247 fixes at a 10-second cadence against a 10-second expected interval, the gaps array is empty and max_gap_sec is 0. None of limbs (a) to (c) is engaged. The excess therefore stands as measured, and the rider does not need the independent corroboration that POL-RD-07(ii) requires only of an impaired trace.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08. Limb (a): the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip id TRP-00304 and the same pickup window, so the artifacts describe the same trip. Limb (b): the excess clears the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. The rider's own profile raises no extra hurdle: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the sub-30% corroboration rule in POL-RD-08 is not engaged — and under POL-GEN-01 no other profile field may be used against her.

POL-RD-03 does not exonerate this route. Limbs (a) and (b) are conceded as far as the advisory goes — LTA advisory ADV-20260806-031 names the PIE eastbound segment Eunos Link to Bedok North Ave 4, and its 17:40 to 21:00 window covers the trip. Limb (c) is what fails: exoneration requires an actual route that leaves the optimal corridor BEFORE the affected segment and rejoins it AFTER it, and the optimal route's own polyline is not in the record. POL-RD-05's notes confirm an amended or substituted optimal must be a stored field and must not be re-derived by the tribunal. The platform's own derived advisory-area block records that the optimal polyline is absent and states in terms that the proxy it computed 'decides nothing by itself'. Limb (c) is therefore not made out, and under POL-RD-08 that is the driver's burden to discharge, not the rider's to disprove.

With no exoneration established, the refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, not discretionary. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 24.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 30.0 optimal minutes) x the 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee = 31.00, with no on-optimal-route ERP (optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00), no properly chargeable airport surcharge (the trip ends at Changi and does not originate there), no waiting-time fee and no promo discount. Refund = charged_total 38.76 less 31.00 = 7.76, and the payable is rounded UP to SGD 7.80. That is far above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and only about 20% of charged_total, well short of the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND — and it exceeds the SGD 6.00 the rider actually contested, so her claim is made out in full.

This is not an upfront-quoted trip, so nothing in POL-RD-11 closes the distance-and-time route. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null; the ~$33 the rider recalls from the booking screen is not a stored quote field on any artifact and cannot be treated as one. POL-RD-11 applies only where the fare model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and a quoted fare is recorded, and neither condition holds, so the POL-RD-02 recomputation above is the governing remedy.

The ECP gantry charge is not the rider's to bear on any view of the case. The trace passes the gantry — the nearest fix is 0 m from the gantry coordinate — so this is a real crossing and not a phantom line, but it is off the optimal route (on_optimal_route false; off_optimal_route_total SGD 1.00). Under POL-RD-09(1) that charge is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, because the recomputed fare includes only gantries lying on the optimal route, and it must never be added on top. If the closure exoneration were applied instead, POL-RD-09(2) still refunds the off-route ERP to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction within the SGD 12.00 cap, because the rider did not cause the closure either. The only question is which route the refund takes, never whether the rider pays for a gantry she never asked to cross.

The driver cannot move this case onto POL-RD-04. The clause requires an instruction that (a) comes from the rider, (b) is timed before the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor or no more than three minutes after, and (c) identifies a place or road specifically enough to act on. The only rider message in the chat log is 'ok', which instructs nothing and names no road; it follows the driver's own message 'PIE closed after Eunos, i take ECP ok' by fifty seconds, so it is assent to a decision the driver had already announced, not a rider-requested detour. waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so the 200 m corroboration test cannot be run at all and, on POL-RD-04's own terms, the clause is unavailable and no distance is excluded under it.

claims.text: The driver's excuse is documented, not asserted. EV-ADVIS-00304-01 is a COMPLETE, full-weight LTA DataMall record of a full closure of the 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Changi, Eunos Link to Bedok North Ave 4', and the trip record's optimal route is 'PIE eastbound throughout' — so the advisory names the very corridor the optimal route traverses, which is POL-RD-03(a). Its validity window, 17:40 to 21:00, brackets the whole trip from the 18:26:59 first fix to the 19:07:59 last fix, i.e. it covers the time the vehicle would have reached that segment with far more than the 15-minute buffer POL-RD-03(b) allows at each end.

The exoneration cap swallows the entire deviation. POL-RD-03 caps the justified excess at min(measured excess, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00 km) = min(4.9, 1.30 x (27.5 - 24.0) + 1.00) = min(4.9, 5.55) = 4.9 km. Because the cap (5.55 km) exceeds the measured excess (4.9 km), the whole excess is justified and the closure-adjusted optimal distance is 24.0 + 4.9 = 28.9 km — exactly the 28.9 km the trace records, leaving zero excess for POL-RD-01 to call a deviation. POL-RD-02 is likewise not engaged: by its own terms it runs only against 'excess beyond that cap', and there is none. The distance and time charges stand.

POL-RD-03(c) is corroborated by the trace, not merely by the driver's word. The fare ledger carries exactly one ERP gantry — 'ECP (Fort Rd towards Changi)' — and it is expressly flagged on_optimal_route: false, while the GPS trace's nearest fix sits 0 m from that gantry (fix index 153, 18:52:29), so the vehicle crossed a gantry the optimal route never uses. The trace also enters the advisory's own area, with 8 fixes inside it. The route actually driven is the diversion the advisory itself directed ('Divert via ECP'), which is the departure-from-corridor pattern POL-RD-03(c) describes.

The rider was not ambushed. EV-CHAT-00304 shows the driver messaging at 18:39:59, 'PIE closed after Eunos, i take ECP ok', and the rider answering 'ok' at 18:40:49, delivered and read at 18:40:59. The rider consented to the ECP route in advance, so the counterparty statement that he told her in chat and she agreed rests on an artifact rather than on his assertion. To the extent that assent operates as a rider instruction — she adopted a message that named the ECP road specifically, and the trace then travelled that road — the deviation is independently exonerated under POL-RD-04 as well.

Even at its highest, the rider's recoverable amount is the single off-route pass-through line of SGD 1.00 for the one ECP gantry, not the SGD 6.00 claimed. Where a closure exonerates the deviation as an external event under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-09(2) refunds off-route ERP as a standalone pass-through correction capped at SGD 12.00 per trip, so the ceiling on this record is $1.00. And because the rider consented to the ECP route, the detour was to that extent rider-caused, so POL-RD-09(3) provides that no ERP refund is due at all. Neither route reaches the sum claimed.

No repeat-deviation uplift can apply. The driver's trailing-90-day figures are deviation_flags_90d = 0 against completed_trips_90d = 260 — a ratio of 0.00, far below POL-RD-06's 0.05 trigger — so neither limb (a)'s resolution of a balanced record nor limb (b)'s FULL_REFUND uplift is available. The uplift is in any event unreachable: the excess here (4.9 km, 20.4%) is well under the 8.0 km and 50% materiality gate that would bring POL-RD-06 into play.

This is a case for a money ruling, not an escalation. The trace is sound for policy purposes: coverage_pct 100, no gaps, and max_gap_sec 0 against a 10-second cadence, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) are not met. The only ERP line is matched to a fix at 0 m, so there is no orphan charge line under POL-RD-10(8); and the exculpatory clause the driver relies on rests on an artifact that is present (EV-ADVIS-00304-01), not missing, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, and the present charge should be left standing rather than held.

The rider's premise of a $33 in-app quote is not in the record: EV-FARE-00304 records fare_model METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11's upfront-quote route — which requires a non-null quoted_fare_sgd — is closed, and the POL-RD-02 metered arithmetic governs. On the metered route, once POL-RD-03 has absorbed the excess, no distance-or-time refund arises; and had the trip been upfront-quoted, POL-RD-11 would bar a distance-or-time refund altogether. The rider is not out of pocket on distance or time on either view.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the raw geometry, and so do I. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00304) runs 28.9 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 24.0 km (EV-TRIP-00304) — an excess of 4.9 km, 20.4% of optimal — so both limbs of the POL-RD-01 test are passed (>0.8 km and >20%), and a deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The trace is sound for policy purposes: 247 fixes at a 10-second cadence, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0, so POL-RD-07(a)–(c) are not engaged and the independent corroboration that clause demands of an impaired trace is not needed. The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry TRP-00304 and the same pickup window.

The deviation is nevertheless exonerated under POL-RD-03. The bundle holds a full-weight LTA DataMall advisory (EV-ADVIS-00304-01) naming the very segment the optimal route traverses — 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Changi, Eunos Link to Bedok North Ave 4' — with a 17:40–21:00 window that brackets the whole trip, and its own text directs 'Divert via ECP'. That satisfies POL-RD-03(a) and (b). For limb (c), the actual route follows the diversion: the only ERP gantry charged is 'ECP (Fort Rd towards Changi)', flagged on_optimal_route false, and the nearest fix sits 0 m from it (fix 153), i.e. the vehicle left the PIE corridor for the ECP the advisory directed. The rider is right that the optimal route's own polyline is not in the record; limb (c) asks whether the actual route took the diversion, and the off-optimal ECP crossing shows that it did.

Exoneration is capped at min(measured 4.9 km, 1.30 × (shortest lawful alternative 27.5 − optimal 24.0) + 1.00 = 5.55 km) = 4.9 km, so the whole excess is justified and no residual distance excess survives. The closure-adjusted optimal is 24.0 + 4.9 = 28.9 km, and its duration is the booked 30.0 min scaled by 28.9/24.0 = 36.1 min. Recomputing the fare against that adjusted optimal: (3.80 + 0.75 × 28.9 + 0.28 × 36.1) × 1.0 (surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 on-optimal-route ERP = 36.38. Your charged total was 38.76, so the refund is 38.76 − 36.38 = 2.38, rounded up to SGD 2.40. The 1.00 off-route ERP line is already comprehended in that figure (POL-RD-09(1)) and is not added on top.

The rider's alternative figure of 7.80 (POL-RD-02 against the booked optimal) is rejected: it assumes the closure is not exonerated, and it is. Her POL-RD-11 point is accepted — the fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so no upfront-quote bar applies, and the ~$33 'quote' she recalls appears on no artifact and cannot be used. The driver's POL-RD-04 (rider-requested detour) argument is rejected as a source of exoneration: the only rider message is 'ok', which assents to a decision the driver had already announced and names nothing, and waypoint_hint is null, so that clause's corroboration test cannot run and it excludes no distance (POL-RD-14 does not apply either, since the route did follow the ECP). The driver's suggestion that the rider recovers nothing, or only the 1.00 ERP, is not accepted for the reason above. No POL-RD-06 uplift is available (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 260 completed trips — no pattern), so no conduct referral fires. There is no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4): the ECP gantry was genuinely crossed, and the trip ends at Changi rather than originating there, so no airport surcharge is chargeable and none was charged. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires — trip ids match, timestamps neither disagree by 10 minutes nor run backwards, the trace is unimpaired, the advisory relied on is present and covers the window, and no charge line is orphaned — and confidence sits well above the 0.70 floor. The amount (2.40) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically.

Confidence is capped under POL-GEN-02(2) at the minimum weight of the artifacts carrying the deciding facts — the GPS trace, trip record, fare breakdown and advisory all sit at weight 1.00 — so the cap is 1.00.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver, here is the decision.

1. A deviation is established. The GPS trace governs distance under POL-RD-01: it runs 28.9 km (EV-GPS-00304) against the 24.0 km booked optimal (EV-TRIP-00304) — an excess of 4.9 km, or 20.4%, clearing both the 0.8 km and the 20% limbs.

2. That deviation is exonerated under POL-RD-03. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00304-01 is a complete, full-weight record of a full closure of the PIE eastbound (Eunos Link to Bedok North Ave 4) — the exact corridor the optimal route uses — and its 17:40–21:00 window brackets the whole trip. The route actually driven matches: the fare ledger carries one ERP gantry, 'ECP (Fort Rd towards Changi)', flagged on_optimal_route false, with the trace's nearest fix 0 m from it, and the trace enters the advisory's area (8 fixes). The rider's argument that limb (c) fails because the optimal polyline is absent is rejected: limb (c) is a fact about the route actually driven, and the trace, the off-corridor gantry, the driver's 18:39:59 chat message and the rider's own account that the driver 'took the ECP instead of PIE' establish that the vehicle left the PIE corridor and ran the diversion. The advisory-area proxy is weighed with those facts, not on its own.

3. Exoneration is capped at min(4.9 km, 1.30 × (27.5 − 24.0) + 1.00 = 5.55 km) = 4.9 km, so the whole measured excess is justified and the closure-adjusted optimal is 28.9 km / 36.1 min.

4. ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver.

The fare was metered, not quoted: EV-FARE-00304 records fare_model METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so the ~$33 you remember from the app is not a stored quote and POL-RD-11 does not apply. You were charged SGD 38.76.

A route deviation is established on the raw figures. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00304, weight 1.0, no issues) runs 28.9 km against the booked optimal of 24.0 km — an excess of 4.9 km, 20.4% of optimal, over both POL-RD-01 thresholds (0.8 km and 20%). The trace is not impaired: 100% coverage, 247 fixes at the 10-second cadence, no gaps, so POL-RD-07(a)–(c) are not engaged.

The driver's explanation is, however, documented, and it excuses the deviation. EV-ADVIS-00304-01 (weight 1.0, no issues) is an LTA advisory for a HIGH-severity full closure of 'PIE towards Changi, Eunos Link to Bedok North Ave 4' from 17:40 to 21:00 on the trip date, directing traffic to 'Divert via ECP'. The booked optimal route is PIE eastbound throughout, so the advisory names the corridor the optimal route uses — POL-RD-03(a). Its window brackets the whole trip — POL-RD-03(b). The trace matches the diversion — POL-RD-03(c): the vehicle enters the advisory's own area (8 fixes inside, minimum distance 0 m) and crosses the ECP (Fort Rd towards Changi) gantry, which EV-FARE-00304 marks on_optimal_route false. The rider's argument that limb (c) cannot be shown because the optimal route's polyline is not in the record is rejected: the departure-and-rejoin pattern is what the trace and the advisory-directed ECP crossing establish, and that is the closest test the record allows.

The exoneration is capped at min(measured 4.9 km, 1.30 x (27.5 - 24.0) + 1.00 = 5.55 km) = 4.9 km. The whole excess is justified; the closure-adjusted optimal (24.0 + 4.9 = 28.9 km) equals the distance actually driven, so no excess remains for POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 does not run. The distance and time lines of the fare stand — the 7.80 the rider's advocate computes on the booked optimal is not payable, and neither is the 2.40 the money block shows against the closure-adjusted optimal, because no excess remains beyond the cap for POL-RD-02 to refund.

One charge is returned. The only ERP line, ECP (Fort Rd towards Changi), SGD 1.00, is a real crossing (nearest fix 0 m) but it is off the optimal route, and the optimal route carries no ERP. Because the deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-09(2) refunds that off-route pass-through to the rider as a standalone correction within the SGD 12.00 cap. The driver's argument that the rider's 'ok' reply made the detour rider-caused, so that POL-RD-09(3) bars even this refund, is rejected: POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction that names a place or road, and 'ok' is assent to a decision the driver had already announced, not a rider-requested detour. The detour is closure-caused, not rider-caused.

Figures: charged_total SGD 38.76; distance/time refund SGD 0.00; off-route ERP refund SGD 1.00; total refund SGD 1.00 — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% full-refund share.

No repeat-deviation uplift applies (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 260 completed trips, and the excess is not material — 20.4% and 4.9 km, under the 50% / 8.0 km gate), so no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. No escalation trigger fires: trip ids match across the artifacts, timestamps do not disagree, the trace has no gaps, the driver's exculpatory clause rests on a present artifact, and the only charge line is matched to the trace. No billing-integrity referral arises because the sole ERP line is a genuine crossing, not a phantom.

Confidence 0.85; every artifact this ruling rests on carries weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0. The monetary effect (SGD 1.00) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold and executes automatically. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal once under POL-GEN-04.

ledger.claim: The deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The GPS polyline runs 28.9 km between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event against a booked optimal of 24.0 km — an excess of 4.9 km, or 20.42% of optimal. Both limbs of the establishment test are passed: the excess is greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure and expressly forbids citing the rounded trip_record copy for the threshold test; here the two agree at 28.9 km, so the finding is safe either way.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: coverage is 100%, there are 247 fixes at a 10-second cadence against a 10-second expected interval, the gaps array is empty and max_gap_sec is 0. None of limbs (a) to (c) is engaged. The excess therefore stands as measured, and the rider does not need the independent corroboration that POL-RD-07(ii) requires only of an impaired trace.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08. Limb (a): the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip id TRP-00304 and the same pickup window, so the artifacts describe the same trip. Limb (b): the excess clears the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. The rider's own profile raises no extra hurdle: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the sub-30% corroboration rule in POL-RD-08 is not engaged — and under POL-GEN-01 no other profile field may be used against her.

POL-RD-03 does not exonerate this route. Limbs (a) and (b) are conceded as far as the advisory goes — LTA advisory ADV-20260806-031 names the PIE eastbound segment Eunos Link to Bedok North Ave 4, and its 17:40 to 21:00 window covers the trip. Limb (c) is what fails: exoneration requires an actual route that leaves the optimal corridor BEFORE the affected segment and rejoins it AFTER it, and the optimal route's own polyline is not in the record. POL-RD-05's notes confirm an amended or substituted optimal must be a stored field and must not be re-derived by the tribunal. The platform's own derived advisory-area block records that the optimal polyline is absent and states in terms that the proxy it computed 'decides nothing by itself'. Limb (c) is therefore not made out, and under POL-RD-08 that is the driver's burden to discharge, not the rider's to disprove.

With no exoneration established, the refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, not discretionary. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 24.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 30.0 optimal minutes) x the 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee = 31.00, with no on-optimal-route ERP (optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00), no properly chargeable airport surcharge (the trip ends at Changi and does not originate there), no waiting-time fee and no promo discount. Refund = charged_total 38.76 less 31.00 = 7.76, and the payable is rounded UP to SGD 7.80. That is far above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and only about 20% of charged_total, well short of the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND — and it exceeds the SGD 6.00 the rider actually contested, so her claim is made out in full.

This is not an upfront-quoted trip, so nothing in POL-RD-11 closes the distance-and-time route. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null; the ~$33 the rider recalls from the booking screen is not a stored quote field on any artifact and cannot be treated as one. POL-RD-11 applies only where the fare model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and a quoted fare is recorded, and neither condition holds, so the POL-RD-02 recomputation above is the governing remedy.

The ECP gantry charge is not the rider's to bear on any view of the case. The trace passes the gantry — the nearest fix is 0 m from the gantry coordinate — so this is a real crossing and not a phantom line, but it is off the optimal route (on_optimal_route false; off_optimal_route_total SGD 1.00). Under POL-RD-09(1) that charge is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, because the recomputed fare includes only gantries lying on the optimal route, and it must never be added on top. If the closure exoneration were applied instead, POL-RD-09(2) still refunds the off-route ERP to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction within the SGD 12.00 cap, because the rider did not cause the closure either. The only question is which route the refund takes, never whether the rider pays for a gantry she never asked to cross.

The driver cannot move this case onto POL-RD-04. The clause requires an instruction that (a) comes from the rider, (b) is timed before the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor or no more than three minutes after, and (c) identifies a place or road specifically enough to act on. The only rider message in the chat log is 'ok', which instructs nothing and names no road; it follows the driver's own message 'PIE closed after Eunos, i take ECP ok' by fifty seconds, so it is assent to a decision the driver had already announced, not a rider-requested detour. waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so the 200 m corroboration test cannot be run at all and, on POL-RD-04's own terms, the clause is unavailable and no distance is excluded under it.

The driver's excuse is documented, not asserted. EV-ADVIS-00304-01 is a COMPLETE, full-weight LTA DataMall record of a full closure of the 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Changi, Eunos Link to Bedok North Ave 4', and the trip record's optimal route is 'PIE eastbound throughout' — so the advisory names the very corridor the optimal route traverses, which is POL-RD-03(a). Its validity window, 17:40 to 21:00, brackets the whole trip from the 18:26:59 first fix to the 19:07:59 last fix, i.e. it covers the time the vehicle would have reached that segment with far more than the 15-minute buffer POL-RD-03(b) allows at each end.

The exoneration cap swallows the entire deviation. POL-RD-03 caps the justified excess at min(measured excess, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00 km) = min(4.9, 1.30 x (27.5 - 24.0) + 1.00) = min(4.9, 5.55) = 4.9 km. Because the cap (5.55 km) exceeds the measured excess (4.9 km), the whole excess is justified and the closure-adjusted optimal distance is 24.0 + 4.9 = 28.9 km — exactly the 28.9 km the trace records, leaving zero excess for POL-RD-01 to call a deviation. POL-RD-02 is likewise not engaged: by its own terms it runs only against 'excess beyond that cap', and there is none. The distance and time charges stand.

POL-RD-03(c) is corroborated by the trace, not merely by the driver's word. The fare ledger carries exactly one ERP gantry — 'ECP (Fort Rd towards Changi)' — and it is expressly flagged on_optimal_route: false, while the GPS trace's nearest fix sits 0 m from that gantry (fix index 153, 18:52:29), so the vehicle crossed a gantry the optimal route never uses. The trace also enters the advisory's own area, with 8 fixes inside it. The route actually driven is the diversion the advisory itself directed ('Divert via ECP'), which is the departure-from-corridor pattern POL-RD-03(c) describes.

The rider was not ambushed. EV-CHAT-00304 shows the driver messaging at 18:39:59, 'PIE closed after Eunos, i take ECP ok', and the rider answering 'ok' at 18:40:49, delivered and read at 18:40:59. The rider consented to the ECP route in advance, so the counterparty statement that he told her in chat and she agreed rests on an artifact rather than on his assertion. To the extent that assent operates as a rider instruction — she adopted a message that named the ECP road specifically, and the trace then travelled that road — the deviation is independently exonerated under POL-RD-04 as well.

Even at its highest, the rider's recoverable amount is the single off-route pass-through line of SGD 1.00 for the one ECP gantry, not the SGD 6.00 claimed. Where a closure exonerates the deviation as an external event under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-09(2) refunds off-route ERP as a standalone pass-through correction capped at SGD 12.00 per trip, so the ceiling on this record is $1.00. And because the rider consented to the ECP route, the detour was to that extent rider-caused, so POL-RD-09(3) provides that no ERP refund is due at all. Neither route reaches the sum claimed.

No repeat-deviation uplift can apply. The driver's trailing-90-day figures are deviation_flags_90d = 0 against completed_trips_90d = 260 — a ratio of 0.00, far below POL-RD-06's 0.05 trigger — so neither limb (a)'s resolution of a balanced record nor limb (b)'s FULL_REFUND uplift is available. The uplift is in any event unreachable: the excess here (4.9 km, 20.4%) is well under the 8.0 km and 50% materiality gate that would bring POL-RD-06 into play.

This is a case for a money ruling, not an escalation. The trace is sound for policy purposes: coverage_pct 100, no gaps, and max_gap_sec 0 against a 10-second cadence, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) are not met. The only ERP line is matched to a fix at 0 m, so there is no orphan charge line under POL-RD-10(8); and the exculpatory clause the driver relies on rests on an artifact that is present (EV-ADVIS-00304-01), not missing, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, and the present charge should be left standing rather than held.

The rider's premise of a $33 in-app quote is not in the record: EV-FARE-00304 records fare_model METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11's upfront-quote route — which requires a non-null quoted_fare_sgd — is closed, and the POL-RD-02 metered arithmetic governs. On the metered route, once POL-RD-03 has absorbed the excess, no distance-or-time refund arises; and had the trip been upfront-quoted, POL-RD-11 would bar a distance-or-time refund altogether. The rider is not out of pocket on distance or time on either view.
